column1: # A label is part of the version string only while its paths still differ
# between upstream/main and the ref being built:
# A difference means the patch is still only on the fork. Patch-id
# (`git cherry`) is not used: upstream squashes, so patch-ids do not match.
# Format: one section per label. The header is the label and a colon.
# The following lines are repo-relative paths (files or directories) that
# belong to that label. A blank line ends nothing; the next header starts
# the next label. A line whose first non-space character is # is a comment.
# Alternatively, one path per line as <label><TAB><path>.
# Label order in the version string is the order of first appearance here.
# - A path that differs from upstream/main and matches no label stops the
#   build (exit 4). Name it here, or drop the fork-only change.
# - When the ref is main or origin/main, a label whose paths do not differ
#   from upstream/main stops the build (exit 6, herding-vicuna#42). The
#   patch was likely absorbed upstream; remove the label from this file.
